title: TP-Link Archer Command Injection Flaws Enable Root-Level Code Execution
content_md: TP-Link has disclosed three high-severity command injection vulnerabilities affecting Archer BE800 V1, Archer BE3600 V1, and Archer AX75 V1 routers. Tracked as CVE-2026-9254, CVE-2026-16348, and CVE-2026-78541, the flaws could allow attackers to execute arbitrary operating-system commands with root privileges. The most severe issue, CVE-2026-9254, affects the parental-control functionality in all three router models. The vulnerability stems from insufficient filtering and neutralization of special characters in certain parameters. TP-Link Archer Command Injection Flaws A LAN-based attacker does not need authentication to exploit the flaw, provided they can reach the vulnerable device from the local network. TP-Link assigned CVE-2026-9254 a CVSS v4.0 score of 8.7, rated High. Successful exploitation can lead to complete device compromise, allowing an attacker to affect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of both the router and traffic passing through it. Root-level execution on a network gateway could enable traffic interception, DNS manipulation , configuration changes, malicious firmware-related activity, or further attacks targeting connected systems. The second vulnerability, CVE-2026-16348, is an authenticated command injection flaw in the VPN connection functionality of Archer BE800 V1.
